mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 30 days compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as market participants anticipate lower cost of capital.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >60% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines by >0.25pp over 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sub-3.5% unemployment rate signals tight labor market conditions that elevate consumer spending and corporate profit margins, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in >50% of periods where UNRATE remains below 3.5% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous FEDFUNDS decline (>0.25pp) and CPIAUCSL stability (<0.5pp change) indicate policy accommodation without inflationary risk, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >60% of cases where FEDFUNDS declines >0.25pp and CPIAUCSL change < 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions (GDPC1 growth >3.0% YoY), rising HOUST signals sustained housing demand that correlates with elevated consumer spending and positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative in >50% of periods where HOUST rises >2% and GDPC1 growth exceeds 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained INDPRO increase (>1.5% monthly) reflects strengthening manufacturing output that correlates with rising corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >60% of instances where INDPRO rises >1.5% over 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL inflation exceeding 3.0% annually triggers expectations of aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days as discount rates rise.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in >60% of periods where CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent RSAFS growth (>1% monthly) and HOUST expansion (>1% monthly) signal robust consumer demand that drives positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are negative in >50% of periods where RSAFS and HOUST both rise >1% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: In high-employment regimes (PAYEMS > 150M), a sub-4.0% unemployment rate sustains corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >50% of instances where PAYEMS exceeds 150M and UNRATE remains below 4.0%.
